verdict.tagline: Promising action RPG mechanics weighed down by server issues and technical hiccups.
for_you_if: you want deep crafting systems and flexible loot filters
you value available offline single player modes
not_for_you_if: you rely on stable server connections during sessions
you expect working controller support out of the box
you want polished performance without heavy loading times

claims.claim: Reviewers report that controller support is poorly implemented, noting that certain buttons fail to work, menus can cause the player to get stuck, and key bindings cannot be customized.

citations.review_text:
Impossible de modifier la touche A de la manette. Je comprendrais J A M A I S ce qui passe par la tête des gens qui font ça.
Encore des développeurs qui se sont dit qu'il fallait surtout pas que les joueurs décident. Ils sont tellement stupides, vous comprenez, c'est pour leur bien. Mais il ne faut pas le voir comme du mépris ou de la condescence, c'est simplement un constat affectueux et qui pousse les développeurs à tout faire pour protéger les joueurs d'eux-mêmes. 

Les devs, puisque manifestement vous savez mieux que moi ce qui est bon pour moi, vous pouvez passer chez moi récupérer mon PC ? L'utiliser librement me met une énorme pression, je me sentirais mieux si vous décidiez à ma place. Si vous pouviez en profiter pour mettre des embouts en plastique sur les coins de tables et de meubles, histoire que je me blesse pas. Et j'aurais le droit de vous appeler daddy ?

Sérieux mais putain, on n'envoie pas des fusées dans l'espace, on joue à un jeu vidéo, et celui-là en particulier me demande moins d'investissement intellectuel qu'un short Youtube. C'est précisément pour ça que je l'ai choisi. Alors putain, ça va, je pense que vous pouvez laisser un tel pouvoir entre les mains des joueurs, celui de remapper une putain de touche. Je sais que les conséquences pourraient être désastreuses (forcer le joueur à cliquer sur "Reset", et là je comprends que vous doutiez de notre capacité à exécuter cette prouesse homérique), mais vous savez, l'oiseau fait tomber les oisillons hors du nid pour leur apprendre à voler, et si vous me donnez du poisson un jour je vais jamais apprendre à pêcher. Insérer n'importe quel autre truc condescendant qui ferait passer des colonialistes pour des émissaires pour l'égalité des peuples.

Sinon, bon jeu.

very unintuitive.
poor controller support.
very poor character design

Pretty good game, the reason I RECOMMEND this game is: there is NO DRM, no requirement for online connection, no restriction for steam client. There are far too few games that give you that amount of freedom and for that I can overlook some of the flaws of the game. They are also planning on split screen coop.

It’s fun in the way that D3 is fun, but more complex. If you’re looking for a D3 clone without BS then it’s the game for you. 

I’ve played 3 classes so far, with 3 subclasses and I’ve experimented with different builds. I feel a little bit more freedom than I did in D2, way more than D3. You can clear content without a build guide, which I also really like. The skills are interesting enough to make me want to see how they interact. I’m not a super invested gamer so it’s just enough to make me enjoy playing. 

There isn’t many flaws worth mentioning because of the things I said before. One I will say is, the controller support is pretty awful, some menus I get stuck so I use the right stick then I get stuck again. It’s frustrating. If there’s a controller connected then there needs to be a discrete controller setting. With 0 need for a mouse pointer. The layout should support that. I can get past this though, it’s really just an inconvenience.

All in all, a gem in a sea of shit, POE2 is for hardcore players which I respect a lot. I am really happy with this game and the way things are going. I don’t mind buying extra content or classes.

FORGET ABOUT playing on a controller.  Half the buttons don't work, it's not intuitive, and just not designed for that type of game play.  On a K/M, the click and drag of skills, sometimes works.  There's NO custom key binding.  The graphics at ultra settings on 5090 looks like they're from PS3 gen (or gives mobile game vibes). Another mid-ARPG, with so many bugs, not even its spells can kill them all.  And I get it, this might be a smaller studio.  But playing DOS I from Larian when they were still a small studio, is a much more premium experience - that it still holds up to this day.  This game is a pass.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as exceptionally easy, lacking any meaningful threat or challenge during early leveling and boss encounters.

citations.review_text:
My biggest complaints/cons with this game are this:

-Combat has no weight. I think its a sound/animation thing where nothing has any gravitas or impact. 
-The difficulty is stupid easy... like brain dead easy to the point where its just not even fun. When there is zero threat from  enemies of chucking your health or one shots, the game becomes stale and boring, and no I don't want to  have to wear boots that nerf me, its mind boggling that that is an option.  Make the game more challenging, or give it a hard, elite, expert, veteran, hardcore, whatever you want to call it. Or just make the game harder more challenging. 
-There is just something off with  the way you move and swing your weapons, and it just feels off compared to  something like POE 2. Its probably because the game wasn't meant for WASD and its a patchwork implementation, so it feels bad. 
- There is a lot they are doing right here, it just feels cheap, like low budget compared to Poe/Poe 2. 
-Items and weapons and there stats are very bloated and non meaningful. The stats in the game have less meaning and direction. Lets call it uninspiring. 

Pros
- All I have said before really sucks even more and is a shame, when you realize they did a really good job with classes and character progression. Or at least so much better the Diablo 4, which is horrendous and so linear and shallow its crazy. 

TLDR
The skills and classes are really great but I wish they would just fix the combat and difficulty, or lack there of. Id play it if they fixed it, but in this current state, ill just play Poe 2, its objectively better in every way.

pros:
-the game feels smooth af
-stash tabs are free
-skills are straight forward which is a pro for newbies , and there are a bunch of them so you can play whatever and try out different things
- crafting (?) [depends on the person honestly. the crafting system seems to be way too easy , and in the long run  , I prefer it to actually be somewhat less deterministic and carry out actual knowledge]

cons:
-way too easy campaign. ended up oneshotting through every boss without knowing what I was doing which makes it not fun to some extent.
-the campaign traveling is a huge mess and I dont know why they made it this complicated to understand in what act you are, what zone , etc. the whole theme about going back and forth in time is just so inconvenient and causes more confusion rather than immersion.

Since I have only played the campaign so far , my review will be about campaign as imo campaign should be enough to tell what the game is about , and its insane to me how people hate on poe campaign after having played LE.
Cant not recommend it though as the gameplay is indeed nice.

Easiest of the popular ARPGs by far. 

Went in today completely blind for first play and started in HARDCORE (Season 4).
I said "I'll just play until I die and then get some zzz"...
12 Hours later I have yet to die and mowing down zones as fast as I can run on Lich.
  No Guides. No Build. No Crafting. SSF.   

Lots of ripoffs from PoE and you can tell clearly what aspects got zero effort or just an AI button to do them but for the price it's worth a weekend minimum.
The game is so incredibly easy in the early game that i just couldn't get to ''the end game thats so hard and in depth '' and stopped playing

Outside of the Krafton takeover this game has it's own issues. I feel like this game just tries to be POE lite, but it feels souless. I think they probably had a good idea originally to make an inbetween arpg between diablo and POE, but now that POE 2 has solved a lot of the complexity issues while maintaining content and Diablo has added some build diversity while adding content this game feels aimless. While they do have some build diveristy there isn't that much to the class or skill passive tree. You just pick up defense and your preferred damage type. I still think its a fun setup, but I wouldn't really consider it that more complex than Diablo. 
     The main problem I had with combat was that the skill lack impact, there isn't enough of sound/vfx/animation to make the skill feel impactful. The 2nd problem is there isn't enough difficulty. Through the whole campaign I never felt close to worrying about dying. Boss were barley above rares. Even into mapping there was no difficulty. It just felt boring. 
     The campaign story was not good or cohesive at all. I know story isn't the focus, but this one isn't interesting at all. Supposedly they were going to finish story after 1.0. I couldn't tell if it was done or not.
     I was also surprised how little content there was, for having 4 seasons there wasn't much there. I don't see how they can keep players with 2 seasons a year and so little content within the season. They probably would do better if it was annual expansions. Also I don't see how they are going to compete seasonally now that there is POE 1&2 and D4. It's a more crowded space and nothing I've seen sets this game apart. 
     Also the controller keybinds need updated for menu. There is a popular steam config that adds inventory, character, skill, and passives to long press of d pad. This works great and should be default. The current default of holding select while picking radial option with right stick then hoping you selection doesn't chang…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the left mouse button is hard-wired to movement and cannot be customized.

citations.review_text: The controls for this game are garbage. The left mouse button is hard-wired to "move chacter to mouse pointer". The spell bar is fixed. It one huge frustrating annoyance that's not worth your time. If they put half the effort into allowing customizable controls as they do into making $79.99 cosmetic skins they might have something worth your time.

FORGET ABOUT playing on a controller.  Half the buttons don't work, it's not intuitive, and just not designed for that type of game play.  On a K/M, the click and drag of skills, sometimes works.  There's NO custom key binding.  The graphics at ultra settings on 5090 looks like they're from PS3 gen (or gives mobile game vibes). Another mid-ARPG, with so many bugs, not even its spells can kill them all.  And I get it, this might be a smaller studio.  But playing DOS I from Larian when they were still a small studio, is a much more premium experience - that it still holds up to this day.  This game is a pass.

Pretty good game, the reason I RECOMMEND this game is: there is NO DRM, no requirement for online connection, no restriction for steam client. There are far too few games that give you that amount of freedom and for that I can overlook some of the flaws of the game. They are also planning on split screen coop.

It’s fun in the way that D3 is fun, but more complex. If you’re looking for a D3 clone without BS then it’s the game for you. 

I’ve played 3 classes so far, with 3 subclasses and I’ve experimented with different builds. I feel a little bit more freedom than I did in D2, way more than D3. claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game includes an offline mode that allows single-player progression without requiring an internet connection.

citations.review_text:
If you like Diablo but think it's too casual and boring, but think Path of Exile is too complex than this is the game for you.

The game has easy to understand game guides for mechanics and you can make builds without a guide very easily as skills are locked to classes.

It's a very easy to understand game with satisfying combat and leveling + the gearing seems to be quite simple too.

MAJOR plus point too is that the game actually has an offline mode. Just a shame you can't buy cosmetics for offline mode or swap offline characters to online and vice versa.

My character is close to lvl 60 now and i can tell you 100% that the campaign is really boring and forgettable, nothing really happens and surprisingly there aren't any bosses in it, atleast not ones that are actually memorable. i think i've only killed like 3 bosses so far?

still fun to play, but it feels like im playing POE2 maps and not a story or campaign. So this is def going to be HELLAAA boring if you play every season.

Bought this under the impression that this was a complete product yet its missing the last two chapters despite leaving early access. This NEEDS to be made clear on the product listing. 
Also it being on season 4 exacerbates this issue. why are we already on season 4 and the campaign isn't even done? I also hear of an upcoming expansion and from a quick google search, that leads me to believing that they are going to lock the last two chapters behind that expansion.

By the time you get to endgame in these ARPGs you'll hardly see your skin anyway, so if you don't like it just don't buy em, I personally don't think you'll be missing out on anything. the good tho. It has an offline mode which is great for internet outages and steam deck, its also pretty well optimized and doesn't require a super computer. The build freedom feels really nice compared to the more streamlined build variety of Diablo.

Still, its a great ARPG and one of the better ones but they have been dropping the ball recently.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that characters cannot be customized in appearance or gender.

citations.review_text:
I wanted to love this game but the classes are just meh - I don't like that your character can't be customized. Just feels and play like a game that wants to have an identity but still not sure what it wants to be. On top of that it's online only now which is a deal breaker for me. 

It was a nice run while it lasted I guess.

Boring, this game is boring, very boring, stupid boring. Just... boring.
Failed to interest me, diablo 2 is still better by a mile, not even close.
Premade characters are ugly and uninteresting.

My Rating: 7/10

If you are looking for an ARPG that is not too challenging, this might be a good choice. 
I only played the main campaign, so I can't say anything about the endgame meachanics. 

The good:
+ Character building is fun, this is where the game shines. You can tinker builds and combinations, the progression rate seems well balanced to me, the skill trees are engagning and fun to execute
+ Offers a good variety of characters
+ Very convenient loot filter function
+ I like the Hardcore-Mechanics (You can start a HC-Char but instead of permadeath, you can opt to play on as a non-HC-Char after death)
+ No crucial bugs in gameplay

The bad:
- Story is about what you expect from a (non story-focusesed) ARPG. Doesn't offer much emotional engagement, it was confusing in the first playthrough.
- Game seems incomplete in some spots (Paladin specialization lacks a skill?)
- Gets a bit choppy in some areas, a bit much for my system, long initial loading time
- No character customization (Chars visuals and gender are predetermined)
- Boss fights sometimes don't feel special enough.

cohorts.summary: Longtime players praise customizable loot filters while struggling with repetitive endgame loops, mandatory campaign replays, and server instability.

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent disconnect issues, rubber banding, and server instability during character selection and zone transitions.

citations.review_text: Constant disconnect issues when trying to login at character select screen. Happening for over 24 hours. All troubleshooting attempts failed.
I just love playing, making progress, getting disconnected, losing a bunch of progress and then having to do it all over again.  This game has really gone down hill.

I've been playing this game since 2021, and I have been an avid supporter, both monetarily and vocally with my friends.  I have poured more hours into this game than any others I've played over the past 5 years, except for World of Warcraft.  Every major update, patch, and season brings me new hope that the same issues that I had in 2021 will finally be resolved.  Unfortunately, they have not.  The rubber banding is unbearable; the disconnects are far too often, the multiplayer is still janky af, and number of other qualities of the game are unacceptable for me to play any further.  I am giving up on this game...for now.  It's simply not playable for me on a consistent enough basis to enjoy the game.  And this is the unfortunate part; this game has the bones to be the BEST ARPG on the market.  The loot system, the crafting, the end game, the talent tree, the skilling system, etc... it's just the best out there.  If this game could have the stability of D4 and the danger and difficulty of PoE2, it would be as about perfect of an ARPG as could possibly be built.  The game simply isn't playable.  Adios LE; this traveler is moving on.  I hope to see you in the future with hardware and systems befit your worthiness.

Unstable connection and disconnects especially on loading screen. As a HC enjoyer, this game offers me 0 satisfaction after losing several characters on DCs/crashes/loading between zones. You need to implement a protection as in other games when loading into zones not to get killed in loading screen between zones. My PC or internet connection are not the issues :D

claims.claim: Reviewers describe progression through the mandatory campaign as tedious and repetitive across multiple seasons.

citations.review_text:
The professions and equipment production of this game have their own characteristics, but after playing for a long time, I found that some mechanisms are very unfriendly to players.
1. The creator of this game is mysteriously confident in the plot of the game. After so many seasons, not only the plot is required to open up wasteland, but also the plot is required to practice the trumpet. Now I want to vomit when I play this plot. It is really terrible.
2. Can you imagine that the map of this game is still level-based. What I mean is that you have to read the progress before entering a new map. If the configuration or network is not good, it will be stuck for a while. This seems to be the game mechanism from 20 years ago. Now other games have long since realized seamless connection with the world map. This map setting is really terrible, which greatly affects the rhythm.
3. Although making equipment is a bit interesting, it is impossible for ordinary casual players to make good equipment. It requires a lot of effort to achieve it.
4. When brushing the map in the end game, once you die, you will fail and lose the game rewards. Moreover, this game character does not have the skill of suspended animation. This is a treasure hunting game, not a soul game. I am speechless.
5. There is no upper limit for the hatching value setting, and it can be stacked all the time. However, there is no time limit for game clearance, which will actually give players a strong sense of frustration and achievement, because there are always people showing off higher hatching values, but you don’t know how much time they spent and whether they are smooth. I think racing games that set upper limits are interesting, that is, Diablo’s ladder, which is a very intuitive way to express the strength of your build.

In short, not recommended.

Oh boy, where to begin with this game. At one point, I thought Last Epoch was the future of the ARPG genre, it was a part of my rotation of ARPG games, but, somewhere along the lines Eleventh Hour Games lost the ideas that made their game truly special, I can only speculate that Krafton might have something to do with this, but, I also cant help but feel that this is also EHG losing sight of what made their game different and stand out compared to its contemporaries. Lets start with the big issue, this game does seasons horribly compared to others. Last Epoch is a game about grinding monolith to make number go up, and it has a painfully dreadful campaign to go through, it also is not difficult enough to require a campaign to get online, so like there is 0 redeeming factors as to why I should have to redo the campaign every single season, especially because alot of the seasonal content isnt relevant until 60+ alot of the time. And before anyone compares this to Path of Exile, let me stop you right there, Last Epoch isnt even sniffing a candle on what GGG has managed to do in their time in the genre, POE1+2 makes campaign rerunning feel at least tolerable because their games are tough enough, that you cant reasonably just hop in at end game and know how to play your character, unless you always run the same toon over and over, Last Epoch does not have that level of replayability. In POE you can reasonably tell me that youve played 15k hours of nothing but Righteous Fire, and I would completely understand, if you tell me that youve played 15k hours of any single class on Last Epoch, I would ask why. The class tuning is also hilariously bad, the first several seasons of the game were completely ruined because of Void Knight being a disgustingly bugged class that continues to world first all of EHGs brand new content, usually through bug abuse. None of my review so far is talking about how greedy EHG has became. Basically. All in all, I could go on for a few hundred more…

This game still feels like it should be in early access. The main story isn't even finished. Every season has been focussed on adding more to the endgame than to the story you have to slog through in every season. The NPCs seem lifeless and voice acting is terrible for both the main characters and NPCs.

The game has potential but needs a lot of polish.

I wanted to love this game.  Sold out and sold out.  You've read all of those reviews.  There's very little to recommend the game.  It does the same things all the other ARPG titles do, not generally as well as the other titles.  Starting over every season is not a big deal, but the grind is reminiscent of a Korean MMO.  Expensive cosmetics you cannot really see.  Same boring quest every season.  Changes in item stats are confusing and hard to see the actual impact, making upgrades difficult.  If I had it to do over again, I'd pass on it.  I'd recommend the same.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the built-in, highly customizable loot filter and the crafting system as major positive features.

citations.review_text: Fun gameplay, good story, lots of depth if you want to dig in. The best solution I've seen for providing a loot filter in-game, no external sources needed or weird coding syntax understanding required.

Last Epoch is a Banger ARPG, I have been playing Last Epoch since the beginning and it has been progressively getting better and better each season. It has a cool class build system, Great built in highly customizable Loot Filter, and a really nice Crafting System. It also has a really interesting campaign with some pretty cool enemies and bosses. Can't wait to see what they add next but if you're into Path of Exile or Diablo you should definitely give it a go.

Absolutely worth it if you enjoy Diablo or PoE style games. Unlike PoE, you can create a viable build without following a guide for your first character, at least if you are experienced with this type of game. Compared to Diablo 4, it has more mechanical depth and more options for building different character archetypes.

The game does some very innovative stuff in the genre from in in-depth in-game guide that can be accessed and searched to learn about all the mechanics, to choosing trade or solo factions and getting appropriately rewarded if you choose not to trade, to in-game customizable loot filters, to a simple to understand but flexible crafting system.

Diablo 4 is still the best choice if you've never played a game like this, and Diablo 4 still has the best story. Path of Exile still has the most absurdly excessive amount of mechanical systems to learn. But Last Epoch holds its own alongside those two giants of the ARPG genre, and is a good buy if you've enjoyed either of those other games.
Good ARPG that respects your time. Between D4 and POE2 difficulty wise. Best craft systems out of all ARPGs.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that required data collection terms and privacy policy acceptances prevent offline play or prevent entering the game without agreement.

citations.review_text: Game no longer offline, "offline" mode scraps your data. RIP

I don't like being legally roofied into data collection, I've owned this game for years and decided to come back to give the new season a shot. But you can't play unless you accept their lawyers contract (you can't opt out of and you have to accept to play). This is not the game that was promised in early access. If companies change what was purchased years later, then years later players should have the option to get their money back. Do not purchase, buyer beware.

single_points.text: One reviewer says they cannot balance the game, with some classes feeling like easy mode and others like bashing your head into a wall, and late-game scaling feeling terrible once hitting empowered echoes.

citation.review_text:
they can not balance this game. Some characters/classes feel like easy mode, while others feel like bashing your head into a wall. Early game scaling feels terrible as one level you will be destroying everything, then next level you will get one-shot, or have to spend 5 minutes bashing against the HP bar of a mini-boss. Late game scaling is also terrible, as once you hit "empowered echoes" the game just scales damage like a cliff, and the game does NOTHING to help you understand what is working/failing; there's absolutely no feedback. 

If you maybe enjoy building character after character that will never finish the game, then this might be for you.
